بُرَكٌ Remaining fixed (↓ بَارِكٌ ) at, or by, a thing. (IAar, K.) So in the phrase بُرَكُ عَلَى جَنْب الإِنَآءِ [Remaining fixed at, or by, the side of the vessel], in a verse describing a [gluttonous] man, who swallows closely-consecutive mouthfuls. (IAar.) ―
-b2- (assumed tropical:) Incubus, or nightmare; as also ↓ بَارُوكٌ . (K.) ―
-b3- (tropical:) A coward; and so ↓ the latter word. (K, TA.) ＝
-A2- Also, [and by contraction ↓ بُرْكٌ , as in a verse cited in the M and TA in art. وبص,] A name of the month ذُو الحِجَّة; (AA, K;) one of the ancient names of the months. (AA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
